source: Holton, Mackridge & Philippaki-Warburton, Greek: An Essential Grammar, 2nd ed. (Routledge, 2016), upload afb4adc8 (PDF pp. 44-55 = Ch 12 Conversational features, §12.1-12.3). Copyrighted, no open license: rules restated in our own words; short phrases and word lists only.

sections.title: Politeness and familiarity
sections.rule: The main politeness markers of Greek are listed in the subsections below.

sections.title: The polite (formal) plural
sections.rule: The second person plural is used to address a single person who is unknown or unfamiliar (a passer-by, a taxi-driver) or who is older or of higher status than the speaker. Pronouns and verbs are plural, but a predicate adjective referring to the single addressee stays singular.

examples.el: Σας παρακαλώ, μου λέτε τι ώρα είναι;
examples.en: Please can you tell me what time it is?

examples.el: Μπορείτε να σταματήσετε στην άλλη γωνία, σας παρακαλώ;
examples.en: Can you stop at the next corner, please?

examples.el: Θα είστε στο γραφείο σας αύριο να σας φέρω την εργασία μου;
examples.en: Will you be at your office tomorrow so I can bring you my essay?

examples.el: Αν είστε κουρασμένος ελάτε να καθίσετε εδώ.
examples.en: If you are tired come and sit here.

sections.title: Diminutives
sections.rule: Diminutive nouns and adjectives are common in offers, compliments and requests, to show affection or lessen the imposition on the addressee.

examples.el: Πάρτε ένα μπισκοτάκι (παρακαλώ).
examples.en: Please take a biscuit.

examples.el: Μας φέρνετε μια μπιρίτσα ακόμη και λίγο κρασάκι (παρακαλώ);
examples.en: Can you bring us one more beer and a little wine please?

examples.el: Το κρασάκι είναι ξινούτσικο, ή μου φαίνεται;
examples.en: The wine is a little sour, or is it my imagination?

examples.el: Ωραία μπλουζίτσα, σου πηγαίνει τέλεια.
examples.en: A lovely blouse. It suits you perfectly.

sections.title: The adverb λίγο
sections.rule: In requests λίγο ('a little') softens the imposition.

examples.el: Έλα λίγο αύριο να τα πούμε.
examples.en: Why not come tomorrow so that we can have a chat.

examples.el: Πέστε μου λίγο το όνομά σας.
examples.en: Tell me your name, please.

sections.title: Να-clause
sections.rule: A bare να-clause expresses a polite suggestion or request.

examples.el: Να σε βλέπουμε πιο συχνά.
examples.en: We would like to see you more often.

examples.el: Να σε ρωτήσω κάτι;
examples.en: May I ask you something?

examples.el: Να πάτε μέχρι το περίπτερο και να στρίψετε δεξιά.
examples.en: You should go as far as the kiosk and then turn right.

sections.title: Present tense of the verb
sections.rule: The second person (singular or plural) present tense in a question makes a polite request, like 'can/could you...?'.

examples.el: Ανοίγεις λίγο το παράθυρο;
examples.en: Can you open the window, please?

examples.el: Φέρνετε το τηλέφωνο πιο κοντά;
examples.en: Could you bring the telephone closer?

sections.title: Παρακαλώ 'please'
sections.rule: Any request can carry παρακαλώ, at the start, at the end, or between major phrases. With the plural pronoun (σας παρακαλώ) it is more formal. Παρακαλώ is also the reply to ευχαριστώ ('you're welcome'); an informal alternative reply is Να 'στε καλά ('be well').

examples.el: Παρακαλώ περάστε από το γραφείο μου την Τρίτη το πρωί.
examples.en: Please come by my office on Tuesday morning.

examples.el: Μου δίνετε το βιβλίο σας, παρακαλώ;
examples.en: Can you give me your book, please?

examples.el: Μου φέρνετε παρακαλώ κι ένα καφεδάκι;
examples.en: Can you bring me a coffee too, please?

examples.el: Σας ευχαριστώ πολύ. – Παρακαλώ.
examples.en: Thank you very much. – You're welcome.

examples.el: Να 'στε καλά.
examples.en: Be well (informal reply to thanks).

sections.title: The verb μπορώ
sections.rule: The second person plural of μπορώ, present or conditional, introduces more formal requests.

examples.el: Μπορείτε να μας φέρετε και τον λογαριασμό, παρακαλώ;
examples.en: Can you bring us the bill too, please?

examples.el: Θα μπορούσατε να μου κάνετε αυτή τη χάρη, παρακαλώ;
examples.en: Could you do me this favour, please?

sections.title: The conditional θα ήθελα
sections.rule: The conditional of θέλω, θα ήθελα, is more polite than the present.

examples.el: Θα ήθελα ένα βιβλίο για δώρο.
examples.en: I would like a book for a present.

sections.title: Familiarity
sections.rule: Βρε, ρε and μωρέ ('hey you') attract the attention of someone fairly familiar. They may be followed by συ 'you', the addressee's first name in the vocative, or words such as παιδί, παιδί μου, παιδιά in the vocative. (Pet names: see 12.2.)

examples.el: Ρε συ, πού πήγες χθες;
examples.en: Hey you, where did you go yesterday?

examples.el: Μωρέ Γιάννη, τι λες να κάνουμε;
examples.en: Hey John, what do you suggest we do?

examples.el: Ελάτε και από δω, βρε παιδιά.
examples.en: Come this way, you guys.

sections.title: Proper names and pet names
sections.rule: Many Greeks are known by an everyday first name that differs a little from the official name used on identity cards. Within the family and among close friends, diminutive endings (11.1) give affectionate forms. Usage varies with individuals and families, and some prefer their official name. Alternative forms may correspond to more than one base name. Greek women's surnames are based on the genitive of the father's or husband's surname and are indeclinable; certain types of feminine surname normally appear in an archaic form (masculine -ίδης, -ιάδης, or stressed vowel + -της).

diminutive_pet_forms.note: from the alternative familiar form Νικόλας

feminine_surnames.note: feminine genitive shows stress shift as in άνθρωπος-type nouns; masculine genitive Μητσόπουλου has no shift, as in καλόγερος-type (see 3.11 type (b))

sections.title: Greetings and wishes
sections.rule: Greetings are followed by plural σας when formal or addressed to several people (καλημέρα σας). Many standard wishes use καλός with a noun in the accusative.

greetings_other.note: γεια σου to one person you know well

greetings_other.en: goodbye (lit. may you go to the good)

welcomes_introductions.note: to one person you know well: Καλώς ήλθες! / Καλώς όρισες

welcomes_introductions.el: Καλώς σας βρήκα! / Καλώς σε βρήκα!
welcomes_introductions.en: Good to see you! (formal or to several / familiar to one) - the normal reply

welcomes_introductions.el: Να σας συστήσω τον φίλο μου Θάνο Πετρόπουλο.
welcomes_introductions.en: May I introduce my friend Thanos Petropoulos.
Pleased to have met you / Nice to see or hear you (at the end of a meeting or phone call).

wishes_with_kalos.en: have a good week! (start of the week)
have a good month! (start of the month)
have a good time!, enjoy yourself!
have a good winter! (said at the end of the summer holiday period)

birthdays_name_days.en: happy birthday! (lit. many years); also a general festival wish for Christmas, Easter, New Year
Long life! (lit. may you make them a hundred [years])

other_wishes.en: to your continued success! (lit. and to higher [things])
may (s)he live long for you! (to a parent on a child's birth or at family occasions)
lit. with health! (to a person with something new, such as clothes)
I hope (s)he will get well soon
here's to next year! (referring to an annual event)
